plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked telomerase ribonucleoprotein mechanism & aging-vs-cancer balance chart from Greider & Blackburn (December 1985, Cell 43: 405–413 & 1987/1989 Nature) and Kim et al. & Shay (23 December 1994, Science 266: 2011–2015) shows telomerase's built-in RNA template (TERC) and reverse transcriptase (TERT) adding TTAGGG repeats in germ/stem cells (and reactivated in ~85–90% of human cancers) while remaining silent in normal somatic cells to enforce the ~50-division anti-cancer Hayflick firewall.

teach_overlay.scale: telomerase is a molecular sewing machine that carries its own six-letter thread pattern inside its pocket — keeping stem cells and newborn babies young, while our normal body cells lock the machine away so rogue cells cannot divide into cancer
